---
title: "Writing around a Python analysis"
format: html
execute:
  cache: true
---

A saved Python result can be read without a Python installation. This example
uses the notebook display API and Python's standard library.

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
from IPython.display import display, SVG, Markdown
values = [1, 4, 9, 16]
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-values
#| fig-cap: "Four squared values."
bars = "".join(
    f'<rect x="{20 + i * 55}" y="{180 - value * 9}" width="35" height="{value * 9}" fill="steelblue"/>'
    for i, value in enumerate(values)
)
display(SVG(f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 260 200" role="img" aria-label="Four squared values">{bars}</svg>'))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| echo: false
display(Markdown("| Statistic | Value |\n|---|---:|\n"
                 f"| Minimum | {min(values)} |\n| Maximum | {max(values)} |"))
```

```{python}
#| label: text-summary
print(f"There are {len(values)} observations.")
```

::: {.callout-note}
The browser displays saved outputs. Render locally after changing the analysis.
:::
